newsitem.title: ITALY: BankItaly's Fazio says economy unsatisfactory.
newsitem.headline: BankItaly's Fazio says economy unsatisfactory.

text.p: Italian economic activity is "unsatisfactory" and the slowdown already under way in 1996 worsened at the end of the year, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Saturday.
Fazio said on the basis of evaluations currently available "growth of gross domestic product (GDP) will be a little more than one percent in 1997."
"At the economic level, the level of economic activity remains unsatisfactory," he told an Italian foreign exchange convention.
Fazio's one percent forecast is slightly higher than a Bank of Italy forecast at the end of October.
The government has an official target of 2.0 percent growth for 1997 but Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said recently it was more likely to be 1.2 to 1.5 percent.
Fazio said expectations on the inflation front were improving but warned there was a possible risk from labour costs, output prices and insufficient action to control the budget deficit.
"Forecasts made in December indicate that for the first half of this year inflation will be between 2.5 and three percent," Fazio said.
Preliminary January inflation data showed consumer prices growing at 0.2 percent month on month and 2.6 percent year on year respectively, compared with final December data of 0.1 percent and 2.6.
Fazio said the recent reduction in official interest rates, which follows cuts in 1996, was made possible by actual and expected improvement in inflation.
The Bank of Italy cut its key discount and fixed term advances or Lombard rates 75 basis points last Tuesday, bringing them to 6.75 and 8.25 percent respectively.
